key_insight: DialogPII introduces a multilingual synthetic dialogue dataset designed to detect personal information across many real-world conversation settings.
clinical_relevance: It can help researchers build and test de-identification systems that protect privacy in shared healthcare and other sensitive conversational data.
method: Generated synthetic dialogues for 8 scenarios using large language models.
Curated and localized dialogs across 11 languages, then converted them to speech and re-transcribed with Whisper.
Annotated entity spans via projection and manual correction, and released baseline multilingual NER models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports technical validation through inter-annotator agreement, translation quality evaluation, annotation projection assessment, and benchmark experiments with transformer-based sequence labeling models.
watch_item: Because the data are synthetic and transcription/annotation were partly automated, performance on real-world noisy clinical conversations may differ.
paper_title: DialogPII: A multilingual dataset of synthetic dialog transcripts to detect personal information
